newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia tries Yugoslav army chief for war crimes.
newsitem.headline: Croatia tries Yugoslav army chief for war crimes.

text.p: A Croatian court started proceedings on Tuesday against Yugoslav army commander General Momcilo Perisic, accused of war crimes for ordering artillery attacks on the seaport of Zadar in 1991.

Perisic and 18 other officers of the former Yugoslav army (JNA) were being tried in absentia by the county court in Zadar on the Adriatic coast, six years after the war over Croatia's secession from federal Yugoslavia.

The Croatian news agency Hina said the 19 accused violated international law by ordering and carrying out artillery attacks on Zadar and its vicinity in September and October 1991, committing war crimes against the civilian population.
Prosecutors held Perisic responsible for ordering shellings that killed more than 30 civilians and destroyed 120 cultural, residential and other objects in Zadar, Hina said.

At the time, Perisic had the rank of colonel and was the commander of the JNA artillery academy in Zadar. He later went on to take the top position in the army of current Yugoslavia, comprising Serbia and Montenegro.

Prosecutors produced two witnesses who said they served in the JNA under Perisic's command at the time and confirmed that he personally ordered artillery bombardments of Zadar and the nearby Maslenica bridge.
Croatia declared independence from former Yugoslavia in June 1991, sparking a war that broke out in full force three months later.
Croatia's Serb minority rebelled against Zagreb's independence bid and the then-powerful JNA used the rebellion as an excuse to move in and try to quell the Croatian secession.
In the process, many major Croatian towns including Dubrovnik, Vukovar, Zadar, Sibenik, Osijek, Sisak and Karlovac were randomly bombarded by the JNA.
